lessons.title: Countries
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam look at a big map and travel books in the library.

items.example: Mia wants to visit France next summer.
items.note: Use 'France' to name the country in Europe, and always start it with a capital F.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat wearing a beret next to a small model of the Eiffel Tower in the library

items.example: My uncle works in Germany.
items.note: Say 'Germany' for the country in Europe, and always write it with a capital G.

image.describe: a friendly orange cat standing beside an old stone city gate with tall towers

items.example: We went to Spain last July.
items.note: Use 'Spain' for the sunny country in southern Europe, always with a capital S.

image.describe: a grey cat playing an acoustic guitar under a sunny sky near white houses

items.example: I ate delicious pizza in Italy.
items.note: Say 'Italy' when you talk about the country famous for pasta and pizza.

image.describe: a white cat holding a warm pizza beside a small boat on a canal

items.example: Sam has a cousin in China.
items.note: Use 'China' to name the big country in Asia, starting with a capital C.

image.describe: a brown cat walking along a long stone wall on green mountains

items.example: My best friend is from Japan.
items.note: Say 'Japan' for the island country in Asia, and always use a capital J.

image.describe: a calico cat looking at pink cherry blossom trees near a snow-topped mountain

grammar.title: Countries with in, to, and from
grammar.explanation: Always start country names with a capital letter. Use 'in' for where someone is, 'to' after go or visit, and 'from' for where someone comes from.

practice.prompt: Smarty points to Paris on the map. Which country is it?
practice.explanation: Paris is in France.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the country name at the end: Japan.

practice.prompt: Sam ate delicious pizza and pasta on his trip. Where did he go?
practice.explanation: Italy is famous for pizza and pasta.

practice.prompt: Match each country with the clue.
practice.explanation: Germany and Spain are in Europe, China is in East Asia, and Uzbekistan is in Central Asia.

practice.prompt: Mia wants to travel to Madrid. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Mia wants to ___ Spain next summer.
practice.explanation: Use visit before the name of a country you want to see.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I am from before a country name.

practice.prompt: Sam's uncle works in Berlin. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: My uncle works in ___.
practice.explanation: Berlin is in Germany, and country names start with a capital letter.

practice.prompt: Ask Smarty which country he comes from.
practice.explanation: Use Where are you from? to ask about someone's country.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I visited France and Italy last summer.
practice.answer: I visited France and Italy last summer.
practice.explanation: Visited is the past form of visit, and both France and Italy start with capital letters.

story.hook: Which countries did Mia and Sam visit?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia, and Sam sitting at a wooden library table with a big open map of Europe and Asia

lines.text: Look at this big map in the library!

lines.text: I love maps! I visited France and Spain last year.

lines.text: I want to visit Germany next summer!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Let's read a book about Germany now.

questions.prompt: Which two countries did Mia visit last year?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I visited France and Spain last year.

questions.prompt: Where did Sam go with his parents?

questions.explanation: Smarty says: My friend Leo is from Japan.

mission.setup: Smarty is looking at a map in the library and asks where you are from and where you want to go.

turns.smarty: Hello! I am from England. Where are you from?
turns.hint: Say I am from and the name of a country.

turns.smarty: Nice! Which country do you want to visit? France, Italy, or Japan?
turns.hint: Say I want to visit and choose a country.

turns.smarty: Great! Did you visit Spain or Germany last year?
turns.example: No, I did not visit Spain.
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, and name Spain or Germany.

lessons.title: Nationalities
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Ben, and Zara meet new friends in the library and talk about where they are from.

items.example: My teacher is French, and she is from France.
items.note: Use 'French' for someone or something from France, and always capitalize it.

items.example: Ben has a German friend.
items.note: Say 'German' to describe someone or something from Germany.

items.example: We like delicious Spanish food.
items.note: Use 'Spanish' for someone or something from Spain.

items.example: My favourite restaurant is Italian.
items.note: Say 'Italian' when someone or something comes from Italy.

items.example: Zara likes Chinese tea.
items.note: Use 'Chinese' for someone or something from China.

items.example: Leo is Japanese, and he lives in Japan.
items.note: Say 'Japanese' to describe someone or something from Japan.

grammar.title: Country vs. Nationality
grammar.explanation: Use 'from' before a country (I am from Spain), and use 'be' directly before a nationality (I am Spanish). Nationalities always start with a capital letter in English.
examples: She is from France. She is French.
He is from Japan. He is Japanese.

practice.prompt: Ana is from Spain. What nationality is she?
practice.explanation: Someone from Spain is Spanish.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen carefully to the last word: French.

practice.prompt: Match each country with its nationality.
practice.explanation: Each country has its matching nationality word.

practice.prompt: Leo is from Japan. Complete the sentence: He is ___.
practice.explanation: Someone from Japan is Japanese.

practice.prompt: We ate pasta at a restaurant from Italy. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: It is an ___ restaurant.
practice.explanation: Use the nationality Italian before a noun like restaurant.

practice.prompt: Ben's friend is from Germany. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ben has a ___ friend.
practice.explanation: Use German before friend to show nationality.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Zara's tea.
practice.explanation: Use Chinese to describe tea from China.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Ana.
practice.explanation: Do not use from before a nationality: She is Spanish.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: My friend is Japanese and my teacher is French.
practice.answer: My friend is Japanese and my teacher is French.
practice.explanation: Both Japanese and French start with capital letters.

questions.explanation: Ben says: Our new music teacher is German, and our art teacher is French!

turns.hint: Say My teacher is French or My teacher is German.

lessons.title: The world
lessons.scenario: Smarty opens a big geography book in the library with Omar and Lily.

items.example: Japan is a big island in the sea.
items.note: Use 'island' for land with water on every side, and say 'an island' before it.

image.describe: a small green tropical island with palm trees in bright blue water

items.example: It is hot and sunny in the desert, and there is no rain.
items.note: Say 'desert' for a large, hot place with sand and almost no rain.

image.describe: golden sand dunes under a bright sun with a small cat wearing a sun hat

items.example: Big fish swim in the blue ocean.
items.note: Use 'ocean' for a huge area of salt water, and say 'an ocean' with 'an'.

image.describe: a wide blue ocean with gentle waves and a small sailboat

items.example: There is a tall volcano in Italy.
items.note: Say 'volcano' for a mountain with an opening at the top where hot rock can come out.

image.describe: a tall rocky mountain volcano with a puff of smoke at the top

items.example: France, Germany, and Spain are on a big continent.
items.note: Use 'continent' for one of the seven huge areas of land on Earth.

image.describe: a colourful globe showing large green and yellow continents surrounded by blue water

items.example: A monkey and a tiger live in the green jungle.
items.note: Say 'jungle' for a thick, hot forest with many trees and wild animals.

image.describe: a lush green jungle with tall trees, vines, and a curious cat peeking from behind a leaf

practice.prompt: Look at the land with blue water on every side. What is it?
practice.explanation: An island is land with water all around it.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

There is a hot desert in China.

practice.prompt: It is hot and sunny with sand and no rain. Where are you?
practice.explanation: A desert is hot and sandy with no rain.

practice.explanation: Each word names a big feature of nature.

practice.answer: I saw a tall volcano and a blue ocean.

lessons.title: Languages
lessons.scenario: Smarty helps Tom and Ana read a foreign travel book in the library.

items.example: French is a beautiful language.
items.note: Use 'language' for the way we speak and write in a country, like English or Spanish.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat surrounded by colourful speech bubbles and open books in the library

items.example: Can you speak Italian or German?
items.note: Say 'speak' followed by a language name, like 'speak English' or 'speak Japanese'.

items.example: Can you translate this into English, please?
items.note: Use 'translate' when you change something from one language into another.

items.example: How do you say hello in French?
items.note: Start with 'How do you say…' when you want to know a phrase in another language.

items.example: I see a new Spanish book. What does it mean?
items.note: Ask 'What does it mean?' when you read or hear something and do not understand it.

items.example: I speak a little Chinese and a little German.
items.note: Say 'I speak a little…' when you know some basics of a language, not everything.

grammar.title: Talking about languages
grammar.explanation: Language names use the same word as the nationality and always start with a capital letter: French, Spanish, German, Italian, Chinese, Japanese.
examples: How do you say thank you in Japanese?

practice.prompt: Spanish, Japanese, and German are each a ___.
practice.explanation: Spanish, Japanese, and German are languages.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the language name at the end: French.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with when you use it.
practice.explanation: These phrases help when you read or talk in a new language.

practice.prompt: Tom sees a Japanese message and does not understand it. What does he ask?
practice.explanation: Ask What does it mean? when you want to know the meaning of something.

practice.prompt: Complete the question.
practice.text: Can you ___ Italian?
practice.explanation: Use speak before a language name.

practice.prompt: Ana has a German book and wants to read it in English. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Can you ___ this into English?
practice.explanation: Use translate when changing from one language into another.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.answer: How do you say thanks in Spanish?
practice.explanation: Use How do you say ... in + language.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I speak a little before a language name.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I speak a little German, and I love this language.
practice.answer: I speak a little German, and I love this language.
practice.explanation: German is capitalized, while language is not.

story.hook: Which languages can Smarty and Ana speak?

turns.hint: Start with How do you say goodbye in Italian?

lessons.title: Story words
lessons.scenario: Smarty reads an adventure book aloud to Lily and Ben in the library.

items.example: Once upon a time, there was a young cat in a big forest.
items.note: Start a fairy tale or classic adventure with 'Once upon a time…'.

items.example: One morning, Leo took his map and walked to the station.
items.note: Use 'One morning…' to set the time when an adventure starts early in the day.

items.example: One evening, we sat next to the lake and ate dinner.
items.note: Use 'One evening…' when an event happens at the end of the day.

items.example: They were happy on the island happily ever after.
items.note: Say 'happily ever after' at the end of a fairy tale when everyone is happy forever.

items.example: Smarty read the book to us: The end!
items.note: Say 'The end' to show that your story is completely finished.

items.example: The young girl in the book is a great hero.
items.note: Use 'hero' for the main good character who helps others in a book or film.

grammar.title: Opening and closing a story
grammar.explanation: Open a story with 'Once upon a time', 'One morning', or 'One evening'. Close it with 'happily ever after' and 'The end'.
examples: Once upon a time, there was a strong hero.
They were happy happily ever after. The end!

practice.prompt: How do you start a classic fairy tale?
practice.explanation: Once upon a time is the classic opening for a fairy tale.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: One morning, he found a treasure.
practice.answer: One morning, he found a treasure.
options: One morning, he found a treasure.
One evening, he found a treasure.
Once upon a time, he found a treasure.
practice.explanation: Listen to the time phrase at the start: One morning.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with where it goes.

pairs.right: at the end of the day

practice.explanation: Use opening phrases at the start and closing phrases at the finish.

practice.prompt: Who is the main good person who helps everyone in an adventure?
practice.explanation: A hero is the main good character in an adventure.

practice.prompt: The sun went down and dinner started. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___, we sat next to the river.
practice.explanation: Use One evening for something that happened in the evening.

practice.prompt: Close the fairy tale. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: They were happy on the island ___.
practice.explanation: Happily ever after closes a happy fairy tale.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The young boy is a hero.
practice.explanation: Use a hero for one hero.

practice.prompt: Finish the adventure with these words.
practice.answer: Finally they went home. The end!
practice.explanation: Put The end at the very finish.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: Once upon a time, one morning, a hero went on an adventure.
practice.answer: Once upon a time, one morning, a hero went on an adventure.
practice.explanation: Use Once upon a time and one morning to open an adventure.

story.hook: Who is the hero in Smarty's book?

turns.hint: Say The hero was a boy or The hero was a girl.

turns.hint: Say The end or Happily ever after. The end.

lessons.title: What were you doing?
lessons.scenario: Smarty asks Mia, Sam, and Leo what they were doing in the library yesterday.

items.example: I was reading a book in the library yesterday.
items.note: Use 'I was reading' to say what you were in the middle of doing in the past.

items.example: They were playing a game in the park.
items.note: Say 'They were playing' for an action that two or more people were doing in the past.

items.example: I was reading while Sam was studying.
items.note: Use 'while' to connect two actions happening at the same time in the past.

items.example: Mia was reading and Ben was studying at the same time.
items.note: Say 'at the same time' when two things happen together.

items.example: What were you doing at five o'clock yesterday?
items.note: Ask 'What were you doing?' to find out someone's activity at a past moment.

items.example: It was raining outside, so we were in the library.
items.note: Use 'It was raining' to describe rainy weather in the past.

grammar.title: Past continuous: was / were + -ing
grammar.explanation: Use was or were + verb-ing to show an action in progress in the past. Use 'while' to join two actions happening at the same time.
examples: I was reading while it was raining.

practice.prompt: Smarty wants to know Mia's activity at four o'clock yesterday. What does he ask?
practice.explanation: Ask What were you doing? to ask about a past activity in progress.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
options: I was reading in the library.
practice.explanation: Listen to the weather phrase: It was raining.

practice.prompt: Match the two parts of each sentence.
practice.explanation: Use was with I/it and were with they/we.

practice.prompt: Mia was reading ___ Sam was working on his computer.
practice.explanation: Use while to join two actions happening together in the past.

practice.prompt: Complete Mia's answer about yesterday.
practice.text: ___ a travel book in the library.
practice.explanation: Use I was reading for what you were doing.

practice.prompt: Ben and Leo were in the park. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ basketball in the park.
practice.explanation: Use They were playing for two or more people.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I was reading while it was raining.
practice.explanation: Both actions use was + -ing joined by while.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: We were studying at the same time.
practice.explanation: At the same time goes at the end of the sentence.

practice.prompt: Say the question and answer aloud.
practice.text: What were you doing? I was reading while they were playing.
practice.answer: What were you doing? I was reading while they were playing.
practice.explanation: Use was with I and were with you and they.

lessons.title: A trip story
lessons.canDo: Tell what happened on a trip
lessons.scenario: Smarty tells Omar and Lily about a rainy trip to Italy.

items.example: We got lost in the big museum.
items.note: Say 'got lost' when you did not know where you were on a trip.

items.example: I was late, so I missed the bus.
items.note: Use 'missed the bus' when the bus left before you got to the stop.

items.example: We got lost, but finally we found a map.
items.note: Say 'found a map' when you discovered a map that showed where to go.

items.example: At the station, we met a friendly man.
items.note: Use 'met a friendly man' to tell about a kind person who helped you on your trip.

items.example: I was reading outside when it started to rain.
items.note: Say 'it started to rain' when rain suddenly began during your trip.

items.example: At the end of the journey, we were very tired.
items.note: Use 'we were very tired' at the end of a busy trip.

grammar.title: Past continuous + when + past simple
grammar.explanation: Use the past continuous (I was reading) for a longer action in the background, and 'when' + past simple (it started to rain) for a short event that happened.
examples: I was reading when it started to rain.
We got lost, but finally we found a map.

practice.prompt: Smarty arrived at the bus stop late, and the bus was gone. What happened?
practice.explanation: When you arrive too late for the bus, you missed the bus.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: We were in the park when it started to rain.
practice.answer: We were in the park when it started to rain.
options: We were in the park when it started to rain.
We were very tired at the station.
We got lost and found a map.
practice.explanation: Listen for the phrase: when it started to rain.

practice.prompt: Match each problem with what happened next.

pairs.right: and we walked to the hotel.

pairs.left: At the end of the journey

practice.explanation: Connect each trip event with its result.

practice.prompt: Who helped Smarty find the hotel in Italy?
practice.explanation: A friendly man helped Smarty find the way.

practice.prompt: We did not know the street. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: At first we ___, but finally we found a map.
practice.explanation: Got lost means we did not know where we were.

practice.prompt: We walked all day. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: In the evening, ___.
practice.explanation: Use we were very tired after a long, busy day.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: We met a friendly man at the station.
practice.explanation: Met is the past form of meet.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I was reading when it started to rain.
practice.explanation: Use when before a short past event: when it started to rain.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: We missed the bus and got lost, but finally we found a map.
practice.answer: We missed the bus and got lost, but finally we found a map.
practice.explanation: All three verbs—missed, got, and found—are in the past simple.

story.hook: How did Smarty find the hotel in Italy?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat showing an old paper map to Omar and Lily in the library

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: One morning in Italy, my friend Leo and I went to visit a museum.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Did you go by bus?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: We were late, so we missed the bus! And we got lost!

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Oh no! What happened next?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: We were walking to the station when it started to rain. Suddenly, we found a map and met a friendly man!

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Did he help you?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! He showed us the hotel. At the end of the day, we were very tired, but happy!

questions.prompt: What happened while they were going to the station?

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about a funny or rainy trip.

turns.smarty: On my trip, I missed the bus and got lost! Did you ever get lost on a trip?

turns.hint: Say I found a map or I met a friendly man.

turns.smarty: Were you very tired at the end of the trip?

lessons.title: My trip
lessons.canDo: Tell a short story about a trip
lessons.scenario: Smarty and his friends share their best trip stories in the library.

items.example: Let me tell you about my trip to Spain.
items.note: Start your story with 'Let me tell you about…' to get everyone listening.

items.example: We saw a volcano and an island. It was an amazing trip!
items.note: Say 'It was an amazing trip' to show you really loved your journey.

items.example: The best part was the Italian food.
items.note: Use 'The best part was…' to share your favourite moment from the trip.

grammar.title: Telling a complete trip story
grammar.explanation: Open with 'Let me tell you about…', describe what was happening and what happened using past continuous and past simple, and finish with 'The best part was…' and 'It was an amazing trip'.
examples: Let me tell you about my trip to Japan.
It was raining when we got there, but the best part was the volcano.

practice.prompt: How do you introduce your trip story to friends?
practice.explanation: Use Let me tell you about before your topic.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: It was an amazing trip to Japan.
practice.answer: It was an amazing trip to Japan.
options: It was an amazing trip to Japan.
We missed the bus in Spain.
practice.explanation: Listen to the phrase: It was an amazing trip.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with how it works in a story.
practice.explanation: A good trip story has an opening, events, and a favourite highlight.

practice.prompt: We visited France and met a friendly ___ teacher.
practice.explanation: Use the nationality French before teacher.

practice.prompt: Share your favourite moment from Italy. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ the delicious pizza!
practice.explanation: Use The best part was to highlight your favourite moment.

practice.prompt: Mia speaks some Spanish. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ Spanish, so I translated the menu.
practice.explanation: Use I speak a little before a language name.

practice.prompt: Choose the right phrase to finish the sentence.
practice.text: I was reading a map when ___.
practice.explanation: Use when + past simple (it started to rain) for a sudden event.

practice.prompt: Build the opening sentence.
practice.answer: Let me tell you about my trip.
practice.explanation: Start your story with Let me tell you about...

practice.prompt: Build the closing sentence.
practice.explanation: Use an before amazing because amazing starts with a vowel sound.

practice.prompt: Say the trip story aloud.
practice.text: Let me tell you about Japan. The best part was the island, and it was an amazing trip!
practice.answer: Let me tell you about Japan. The best part was the island, and it was an amazing trip!
practice.explanation: Great job combining all three story phrases!

mission.setup: Smarty wants to hear your own short trip story in the library!

turns.smarty: Tell me about a trip! Start with Let me tell you about...
accept: ^let me tell you about (?:my trip(?: to (?:france|germany|spain|italy|china|japan|uzbekistan|brazil|england))?|france|germany|spain|italy|china|japan|uzbekistan|brazil|england)$

turns.smarty: Ooh! What happened on your trip? Did it start to rain or did you find a map?
accept: ^(?:it started to rain|we found a map|i found a map|we got lost|i got lost|we met a friendly man|i met a friendly man)$

turns.smarty: What was the best part? Finish with The best part was... and It was an amazing trip!
accept: ^the best part was (?:the )?(?:pizza|food|island|volcano|ocean|jungle|desert|museum)(?: and it was an amazing trip)?$
turns.example: The best part was the pizza, and it was an amazing trip.
turns.hint: Say The best part was the pizza, and it was an amazing trip.
